content.content: 1 # Meeting-room booking app — full spec (verbatim from the user; final, no questions allowed) 2 3 Constraints: Use only Node.js built-ins (no npm install). Node v22. Do not use the Fable model. 4 5 Build a meeting-room booking app: an HTTP server `server.mjs` (an ES module, run as `node server.mjs`) that serves a JSON API and a browser page, and keeps its data in one JSON file. 6 7 ## Server 8 - At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening, in that order. 9 - It listens on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the `PORT` environment variable. An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1. 10 - Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout. 11 - Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. 12 - The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file ` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening. 13 - After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. The server writes the data file only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes one, never at startup or for any other request, and it never creates folders. 14 - Every change is saved to the data file before its reply is sent: after a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`, the bookings, and the id the next booking will get, are as before. 15 - If saving a change fails (for example because the data file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. In both cases the server keeps running. 16 - Requests that arrive at the same time give the same result as if they had been handled one at a time in some order: of several overlapping bookings sent at once while saving works, exactly one is created and every other one gets 409, and no id is given twice. 17 - Before sending any reply, the server reads the whole request body, if there is one, and discards what it does not use, so the client always receives the reply, the 413 and 415 replies included. 18 19 ## API 20 - The rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`, in that order. 21 - A booking is a JSON object with exactly the keys `id`, `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: `id` is a number, the others are strings. The first booking gets id 1 and each new booking the next integer; an id is never reused, even after deletes and restarts. 22 - Only the parsed JSON of a reply body matters: whitespace and key order in it are free. 23 - A request's path is its request target up to the first `?` (all of it when there is no `?`). Routes compare the path byte for byte, with no percent-decoding and no dot-segment, slash or letter-case normalisation: `/api/%62ookings`, `/api/./rooms`, `/API/rooms` and `/api/bookings/` are none of the paths below. The query, the text after the first `?`, is ignored unless stated, and is decoded as `new URLSearchParams(query)` does. 24 - `GET /api/rooms`: 200 `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}`. 25 - `GET /api/bookings`: 200 `{"bookings": [...]}` with every booking, sorted by date, then start, then room in the order above. When the query has a `date` parameter (as `params.has('date')` says; `?date` with no `=` counts, with the empty value), its value is `params.get('date')` (the first one when repeated) and the reply holds only the bookings on that date; a value that is not a valid date by rule 6 below (the empty value included) gets 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. Other query parameters are ignored. 26 - `POST /api/bookings` with a JSON body holding `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: 201 and the new booking. Other keys in the body are ignored. 27 - `DELETE /api/bookings/`: every path that is `/api/bookings/` followed by a non-empty `` holding no `/` is this route, whatever `` is. content.text:
The suite passes: 317 of 317 tests in about 3.2 seconds, with no `console.log`, `TODO` or `.only`. Every file is at most 345 lines and no function reaches 50 lines. The tests are strong overall. The weak points are duplicated helpers and a few spots where the tests depend on how this particular server stores its data.

**What is strong**
- **Booking rules** (`booking-rules.test.mjs`): the tests would catch typical wrong implementations:
  - Titles padded with spaces at the start fail if the code only trims the end (`trimEnd` instead of `trim`).
  - 41 emoji and 40 decomposed `é` fail if length counts characters instead of UTF-16 code units, or if the title gets normalised.
  - Exact 10000 vs 10001 byte bodies, a body that is over in bytes but not in characters, and a chunked body with no `Content-Length` cover the size limit.
  - Bookings are inserted in the order 10:00, 08:00, 09:00 to check that the conflict message names the earliest one, not the first one stored.
  - Each rule's priority over the next one is checked.
- **List order** (`api-list.test.mjs`): "half" and "full" start at the same time but end differently, so sorting by end time instead of room order fails.
- **Request paths** (`api-routes.test.mjs`): every path in spec line 23 that must not match is tested byte for byte.
- **Startup**: the order of checks is shown with a port that is already taken plus a bad data file. The "one plain stderr line" check also rules out stack traces.
- **Page script**: overlapping list fetches are tested in all four response orders. The fake DOM only has the allowed members, so a script that uses anything else fails.
- **Cleanup**: servers and temp folders are cleaned up in `finally` blocks or `after` hooks.

**Problems**
1. **Server can be left running** (`helpers.mjs:66` and `:73`). When `startServer` gives up (no listening line within 5 s, or wrong stdout), the child process is never killed. It keeps running and the test runner can hang.
2. **Tests assume this server's file format.** The spec lets the format be "a layout of your choice", but several tests write `{"nextId":…,"bookings":[…]}` straight into the file, or assume `{}` is invalid. That happens at `startup.test.mjs:142` and `:159` and at `persistence.test.mjs:30`, `:54`, `:131` and `:164`. If the backend changes its format, these tests break even though the server is still correct.
3. **Duplicated helpers:**
   - `withTmp` and `withServer` are copied in `startup.test.mjs`, `persistence.test.mjs` and, in a slightly different form, `page-static.test.mjs`.
   - Three booking builders do the same job: `booking()` in `helpers.mjs`, the one inside `create()` in `api-util.mjs`, and `booking(id, …)` in `fake-dom.mjs`.
   - `chunkedPost` copies `request`.
   - `setup()` in `booking-rules.test.mjs` copies `fixture()`.
4. **Requirements with no test that a wrong version would fail:**
   - An error-status reply whose body is not JSON should show "Could not reach the server." for POST and for the list. Only the rooms request with status 200 is tested, so code that shows "Request failed." there would pass.
   - Unset `PORT` meaning 3000 is not tested; only empty `PORT` is.
   - Title trimming is only tested with ASCII whitespace. Code that only strips spaces, tabs and newlines would still pass.
5. **Checks stricter than the spec** (`page-static.test.mjs`):
   - Line 307 rejects the word "http" anywhere, but the spec only forbids `http://` and `https://`. A comment saying "HTTP" would fail.
   - Line 311 forbids room names in `app.js`, which the spec does not ask for.
   - Line 289 rejects any `.headers` access, which also flags allowed code like `options.headers`.
6. **Smaller issues:**
   - `api-concurrency.test.mjs:40` and `:54` rely on the tests before them having run (ids 1, 2..31).
   - `booking-rules.test.mjs:37` throws when the server never started, and the temp folder is then left behind.
   - The `JSON.parse` at `booking-rules.test.mjs:94` has no error handling.

## GRADE
Overall: 8/10
Verdict: pass
structure: 8 — helpers are split sensibly (process/HTTP, API fixture, fake DOM), but the API fixture is reimplemented in booking-rules and page-static
naming: 8 — names are mostly clear; `E`, `rej`, `same`, `fx` and `JSON_H` are terse
duplication: 6 — `withTmp`/`withServer` copied in 3 files, 3 booking builders, `chunkedPost` copies `request`, `setup()` copies `fixture()`
size: 9 — all files ≤345 lines, all functions well under 50 lines
errors: 7 — `startServer` leaves the child running on timeout or bad stdout; `setup()` teardown throws when start fails; unguarded `JSON.parse` in `chunkedPost`
tests: 8 — exact spec strings and boundaries, kills trimEnd, code-point counting, sort-by-end and insertion-order mutants; but tied to the server's file format, misses non-JSON error bodies, unset PORT and Unicode trim, and over-checks page-static
security: 10 — no secrets; temp folders under `os.tmpdir()`; children get a clean env
leftovers: 9 — no `console`/`TODO`/`.only`; one stray comment and one redundant assert
